text.text: Run the whole shop from one page. New calls land on the Service calls board; the dispatcher schedules them, a technician takes them, and Mark done closes them out. Parts shows what to reorder and Invoices shows who still owes you. Start with the Dashboard each morning.
Customers
Homeowners and businesses you serve, with what you have billed them and what is still owed.
Service calls
Every repair, tune-up and install, with who is on it, what it costs and the margin.
Parts and stock
What is on the trucks and shelves, what it costs and what needs ordering.
Invoices
What has been billed, what is paid and what is overdue.
Open calls, money in and money owed at a glance. Anything under Overdue needs a phone call today.
Overdue service calls
My service calls
Overdue invoices
Follow the same ten minutes at every door. Customers remember the walk-in and the walk-out more than the repair.
Before you leave the shop
Read the call notes and the last visit on this address.
Load the parts the problem most likely needs: capacitor, igniter, filter, contactor.
Text the customer your arrival window and your name.
At the door
Introduce yourself, put on shoe covers and ask where the system is.
Ask what happened and when, before touching anything.
Check the thermostat, filter and breaker first. Half of all no-heat calls end there.
Before you start work
State the repair price in plain terms and get a yes. If the price is above the quote, stop and call the office.
Closing the call
Show the customer what you replaced and keep the old part until they have seen it.
Mark the call done, fill in parts cost and hours.
Hand over the invoice and mention the maintenance plan once, politely.
Plans smooth the slow months. Each plan means two visits a year, one for heating in early fall and one for cooling in spring.
What a plan includes
Two tune-up visits a year
Priority scheduling during hot and cold spells
A discount on repairs
A reminder text two weeks before each visit
Scheduling visits
On the first of each month, add a Maintenance plan visit call for every plan holder due that month.
Group visits by neighborhood so one technician can do five in a day.
Text the customer a reminder. Reschedule within the week if they miss it.
Renewing
Plans renew by card each year. If a card fails, the customer shows under Awaiting payment on their record. Call, do not email.
Count the truck stock every other Friday and the shelves the last Friday of the month. The Reorder? column does the thinking.
How to count
Pick one truck or shelf at a time and count every part on it.
Type the number into On hand and update Last counted.
Anything that says Reorder goes on the supplier list that afternoon.
Reorder rules
When a supplier is out
Ask for the closest equivalent, write the swap in the call notes and tell the customer.
